title: Air-fryer roast beef
subtitle: A small joint of beef roasted in the air fryer with a proper crust.
excerpt: A beef sirloin joint cooked in the air fryer at high heat for a browned crust, then finished at a lower setting to the internal temperature you want. Serves four with resting time included.
sourceNotes: Roast beef is a centrepiece dish of British Sunday cooking. Sirloin is well-suited to air fryer roasting as the fat cap bastes the joint as it cooks. This method produces the crust of a traditional oven roast in significantly less time.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Take the joint out of the fridge an hour before cooking so it cooks evenly from the centre.

content.text: Roast beef in the air fryer works by searing at 220°C for the first 10 minutes to set the crust, then dropping to 160°C to finish the centre without overcooking the outside. An instant-read thermometer is the only reliable way to hit the doneness you want: 52°C for rare, 57°C for medium-rare, 65°C for medium. The joint must rest for 15 minutes after cooking or the centre will be a different doneness to what the thermometer showed.

items.prepNote: tied joint, brought to room temperature

content.text: Pat the {{beef-sirloin}} joint completely dry with paper towel. Rub with {{olive-oil}} of oil, {{sea-salt-flakes}} of flaked salt, and {{black-pepper-ground}} of cracked pepper. Preheat the air fryer to 220°C. Place the joint fat-side up in the basket. Cook at 220°C for 10 minutes until the surface is browned and the fat cap has started to render.

Drop the temperature to 160°C and cook for a further 15-25 minutes, checking the internal temperature every 5 minutes. Pull at 52°C for rare, 57°C for medium-rare, 65°C for medium. Transfer to a board, tent loosely with foil, and rest for 15 minutes before carving. The internal temperature will rise by 3-5°C during resting.

items.cause: Left at 220°C too long or didn't drop the temperature.
items.fix: Only 10 minutes at the high sear temperature. The centre cooks on carry-over heat while you reduce the setting.

items.cause: Fat dripping onto the heating element.
items.fix: Add a splash of water to the drip tray before cooking. Empty and wipe between batches.

items.cause: Most domestic air fryers fit up to around 1 kg at most.
items.fix: Use an 800 g joint rather than a full 1.5 kg roast. For larger joints, the conventional oven is the better tool.

content.text: Air-fryer roast beef is a proper Sunday roast without the two-hour wait. Serve with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes, and horseradish cream. The dripping from the tray is worth collecting: it adds flavour to roast potatoes or fried bread.
